media:group.media:title: The Brutal Battle of Hamburger Hill Ends #thewarofficepodcast #history
media:group.media:description:
The brutal Battle of Hamburger Hill finally came to an end on May 20, 1969 after nine days of combat between paratroopers of the 101st Airborne Division and troops of the North Vietnamese Army's 29th Regiment.
The hill's jungle had been blasted off from the constant bombardments and heavy fighting.

media:group.media:title: First Contact at the Battle of Hamburger Hill #thewarofficepodcast #history
media:group.media:description:
First Lieutenant Frank Boccia's 1st Platoon, D Company, 3rd Battalion, 187th Infantry Regiment of the 101st Airborne Division is the first unit to make contact with the enemy during the Battle of Hamburger Hill.
Boccia recalled the first attack by the NVA in his memoir of the Vietnam War in The Crouching Beast: A United States Army Lieutenant's Account of the Battle for Hamburger Hill, May 1969.

media:group.media:title: The Bombardment on Tskhinvali, South Ossetia Begins #thewarofficepodcast #history
media:group.media:description:
As tensions between Georgia and the breakaway region of South Ossetia have been growing, Georgian military forces begin their offensive to bring the region back under their sovereignty.
On 7 August, the opening bombardment on Tskhinvali, the capital of South Ossetia, starts with more than 100 heavy mortars, artillery pieces and Multiple Launch Rocket Systems opening fire.

entry.title: Black Hawk Super Six Four Shot Down #thewarofficepodcast #history

media:group.media:title: Black Hawk Super Six Four Shot Down #thewarofficepodcast #history
media:group.media:description:
Chief Warrant Officer Mike Durant pilots Super Six Four during the Battle of Mogadishu. The helicopter is hit by RPG fire, just like Super Six One before it.
This helicopter is the second Black Hawk shot down in the battle. Durant survives the crash and is taken prisoner by the Somalia National Alliance militia.

entry.title: Black Hawk Super Six One Shot Down in Mogadishu #thewarofficepodcast #history

media:group.media:title: Black Hawk Super Six One Shot Down in Mogadishu #thewarofficepodcast #history
media:group.media:description:
During a raid to capture advisors of Mohamed Farrah Aidid, the leader of the Somali National Alliance, Black Hawk Super Six One was shot down during the Battle of Mogadishu. Pilots Chief Warrant Officers Cliff ‘Elvis’ Walcott, and Donovan ‘Bull’ Briley pitched the helicopter's nose down purposefully at the last second, ensuring that the pilots absorbed the impact, saving the lives of the crew in the back.

media:group.media:description:
In August 2008, Georgian forces moved into the breakaway region of South Ossetia to assert its sovereignty over the area. Did Moscow orchestrate this move to gain more control and influence in the Caucasus or is Georgia to blame?
Assigning responsibility for the outbreak of the war remains a highly contested and controversial topic.

In March 2002, coalition forces launch Operation Anaconda, an ambitious offensive to destroy entrenched al-Qaeda and Taliban fighters in Afghanistan's Shah-i-Kot Valley. Poor intelligence, difficult terrain, and determined resistance quickly turned the operation into a fierce firefight. Amid the chaos, Technical Sergeant John Chapman fights with extraordinary courage on Takur Ghar, actions that will ultimately earn him the Medal of Honor.
